- Today, Maggie Chi, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Health, and the Honourable Adam van Koeverden, Secretary of State (Sport), on behalf of the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, announced $6 million in continued support to ParticipACTION, helping Canadians of all ages make physical activity a part of everyday life.
- MP Mona Fortier and Mayor Mark Sutcliffe announced over $30 million through the Build Communities Strong Fund to improve electrical reliability at the ROPEC wastewater treatment plant.
- Maggie Chi, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Health, and the Honourable Adam van Koeverden, Secretary of State (Sport), on behalf of the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, will hold a news conference to announce funding to support increasing physical activity rates in Canada.
- Public Services and Procurement Canada wishes to advise users that the Chaudière Crossing will be fully closed to motorists to accommodate rehabilitation work as part of the Southern Structures Renewal Project.
- Skills Development Fund investments will prepare 400 workers and jobseekers for in-demand careers in the skilled trades, agriculture and long-term care
- The Departments of Health and Environment will continue monitoring avian influenza in Nunavut, though no recent cases have been reported.
- The Department of Health is reminding residents that as of August 27, 2026, the following drinking water advisories remain in effect.
- On August 25, the Department of Transportation and Infrastructure Nunavut (TIN) became aware of a reported fuel spill on Baker Lake.
- Residents of Grise Fiord are advised to boil their water until further notice due to high turbidity.

- The Government of Canada is helping the pork industry develop tools to safeguard animal health against infectious disease and strengthen the sector's resilience and growth.
- On September 3, 2026, Rodney Allen, an inmate from Bath Institution’s Regional Treatment Centre, died while in our custody of apparent natural causes.
- Agriculture Minister Heath MacDonald will announce federal investments in animal health surveillance in Charlottetown, PEI, alongside the Canadian Pork Council and the Atlantic Veterinary College.
- The Government of Canada is investing over $13 million through the Youth Mental Health Fund to strengthen youth mental health research and deliver evidence-based care across the country.
- Cancer is the leading cause of death in Canada, with an estimated 254,100 new diagnoses and 87,900 deaths expected in 2026.
- Province investing $3.4 billion to connect everyone in Ontario to a family doctor or primary care team by 2029
- Renovated facility will have 60 new beds for people with complex mental-health disorders
- Applications are open for the 2026-27 Community Addictions Prevention and Mental Health Promotion Grant Program.
- Auditor General Denise Hanrahan delivered a performance audit on long term care facilities to the Public Accounts Committee.
- The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development is replacing automated external defibrillators in schools across the province so students and staff can respond to cardiac arrest.
- The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador issued a public disposal tender for a large air-supported dome structure originally procured for the cancelled Kenmount Crossing Acute Care Campus project.
- The Department of Health advises residents of Arviat that the boil water advisory is lifted.
- The Department of Health is warning about a food recall issued by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) due to possible Listeria contamination.
- Starting September 1, 2026, the departments of Health and Education will resume the toothbrushing program in Arctic Bay and expand it to Gjoa Haven, Naujaat and Iqaluit, highlighting our shared commitment to children's health and community well-being.
- Following dog attacks in several Nunavut communities, which have resulted in serious injuries for those bitten, the Department of Health advises all Nunavummiut to be aware of the risks and asks parents to have conversations with their children about safe interactions with dogs.

- Canadian farmers need modern tools to protect their crops and stay competitive.
- Doug Eyolfson, MP for Winnipeg West, announced on behalf of the Minister of Health and with the Chief Public Health Officer of Canada, Dr. Joss Reimer, a $5 million investment to improve HIV prevention and support services.
- On World Suicide Prevention Day, we renew our commitment to preventing suicide, to supporting people who may be struggling, and to creating spaces for open, compassionate conversations that can help save lives.
- A Request for Proposals has been issued for a review of the role of nurse practitioners in Newfoundland and Labrador to improve access to care.
- The Department of Health reminds Nunavummiut that fall and the return to school often bring an increase in viral illnesses, including flu, COVID-19, hand foot and mouth disease, colds and stomach bugs, including norovirus.
- The Department of Health has arranged alternative accommodations for prenatal patients at Larga Kitikmeot, which is seeing high volumes, while a new boarding home is built.
- Residents of Rankin Inlet are advised to boil their water until further notice due to repair work on the utilidor.

- Ben Carr, Member of Parliament for Winnipeg South Centre, on behalf of the Honourable Heath MacDonald, Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food, will be at Discover Agriculture on the Farm to announce investments that aim to promote health and safety on farms across Canada.
- Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) wishes to advise users that the Chaudière Crossing will be fully closed to motorists to accommodate rehabilitation work as part of the Southern Structures Renewal Project.
- First-in-North America custom splints created at Vancouver General Hospital
- After 10 years of planning and nearly three years of construction, Aqqusariaq, the 24-bed addictions and trauma recovery facility in Iqaluit, is entering the final stages of construction and operational preparations ahead of welcoming Nunavummiut.
- The Department of Health is calling on local, regional and hamlet organizations across Nunavut to submit proposals for one-time funding to support community-led food skills projects.
- The Department of Health is reminding residents that as of September 17, 2026, the following drinking water advisories remain in effect.
- The Department of Health is warning about a food recall issued by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) due to possible norovirus contamination.
- The Department of Health is warning about a food recall issued by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) due to possible Listeria contamination.
- Residents should promptly report suspected bed bugs to the Department of Health and the Nunavut Housing Corporation so inspection and treatment can happen before the infestation spreads.
- The Department of Health has expanded its bassinet program, which is now available in all three regions of Nunavut.

- Today, the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, announced an $80 million investment, over four years, to the Terry Fox Research Institute (TFRI) for its work in precision oncology research.
- The Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, will announce an investment to advance research and personalized cancer care.
- On World Alzheimer’s Day, the Minister raises awareness of dementia and highlights Canada’s latest national dementia strategy report and the authorization of two new treatments for mild cognitive impairment or early-stage Alzheimer’s disease.
- DFO reminds harvesters to check the SHELLI map before every harvest, since shellfish from closed areas can carry unseen contaminants, bacteria, viruses, or marine biotoxins that cause serious illness.
- The governments of Canada and Manitoba are celebrating the 12th annual Farm and Food Awareness Week from September 20 to 25, an opportunity for Manitobans to learn where their food comes from and recognize the work local producers do to bring safe, healthy food from farm to table, federal Agriculture and Agri-Food Minister Heath MacDonald and Manitoba Agriculture Minister Ron Kostyshyn announced t
- Investing in safety training, health awareness, and practical tools helps keep Canadian farmers, their families, and farm workers safe.
- The Government of Canada is committed to supporting people in Canada who have experienced a serious and permanent vaccine-related injury through the Vaccine Impact Assistance Program (VIAP) and to providing claimants with the information they need to navigate the process more easily.
- Province supporting 192 more long-term care spaces in the community while creating good-paying local jobs
- Seniors with the highest risk of serious illness from RSV will get free vaccine starting next week
- Minister Joedy Wall will highlight health care initiatives in Corner Brook on Friday, September 25.
- The Department of Health invites Nunavummiut to recognize World Rabies Day on September 28, 2026, with the theme 'Stronger Together'.
- The Department of Health advises residents of Chesterfield Inlet that the boil water advisory is lifted.

- Residents of Baker Lake are advised to boil their water until further notice due to high turbidity.
- The Environment and Health departments confirmed Nunavut's first avian influenza case since December 2024, detected in birds found near Frobisher Bay and Iqaluit.

- October 5, 2026 Health Data Research Network Canada (HDRN Canada) and the Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) formalizing their commitment to work together to strengthen Canada’s health data ecosystem.
- People encouraged to protect themselves, loved ones from influenza, COVID-19, other viral illnesses
- To help shape oral health programs and make dental care better for Nunavummiut, the Department of Health wants to hear from you.
- The Environment and Health departments are investigating suspected avian influenza in four bird species found dead near Iqaluit between September 4 and 11, 2026, pending confirmatory test results.
- October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to learn about breast health, share knowledge and show support for those affected by breast cancer.
- Residents of Taloyoak are advised to boil their water until further notice due to a mechanical pump failure at the water treatment plant.

- The Department of Health is recognizing October 15 as Pregnancy and Infant Loss Remembrance Day in Nunavut.
- Nunavut is marking World Mental Health Day with the theme 'Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change.'

- The Honourable Sean Fraser, Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada, and the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, will hold a media availability on updates to Canada’s medical assistance in dying (MAID) law.
- The Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, will announce the first recipients of the Canada Research Training Awards and the most recent results of the federal government’s largest funding program for health research.
- Today, the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, announced more than $6 million in funding under the Substance Use and Addictions Program and the Supporting Community Mental Health Crisis Response Initiative.
- Today, the Honourable Marjorie Michel, Minister of Health, announced more than $6 million in funding under the Substance Use and Addictions Program and the Supporting Community Mental Health Crisis Response Initiative.
- Province’s $17 million investment will connect more people to high-quality hospital care, closer to home
- The Department of Health is reminding residents that as of October 22, 2026, the following drinking water advisories remain in effect.
- The Department of Health is advising Nunavummiut of an increase in gastroenteritis, a usually viral stomach flu that causes nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
- Winter is all about layers and the Department of Health is encouraging Nunavummiut to Layer up and get vaccinated.
- Iqaluit health services is seeking three community members to join the client and community engagement team to work with Iqaluit health services staff and leadership on improving health-care services for Nunavummiut.

- For Canadians facing an incurable illness and intolerable suffering, medical assistance in dying (MAID) must remain a voluntary, personal choice free from external pressure and protected by rigorous safeguards.
- Collaboration between Indigenous Fishery Guardians and Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) is vital to protecting vulnerable marine species and the long-term health of Canada's aquatic ecosystems, especially in remote areas.
- Public Services and Procurement Canada wishes to advise users that the Chaudière Crossing will be fully closed to motorists to accommodate rehabilitation work as part of the Southern Structures Renewal Project.
- $3.4 billion Primary Care Action Plan has connected over 511,000 more people to care, on track to attach everyone by 2029
- Flu and COVID-19 immunizations are now available to the general public
- The Newfoundland and Labrador government released a core staffing review aimed at strengthening supports for front-line health care workers and improving access to care.
